description: Re-platform a .NET application's database from SQL Server 2019 to PostgreSQL 16. The database is 500GB with 300 tables, 150 stored procedures (T-SQL), and 80 SQL Agent jobs. The migration must follow: T-SQL dialect rewrite (stored procedures to PL/pgSQL, ISNULL to COALESCE, GETDATE to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP), permission model migration (SQL Server logins/roles to Postgres roles/grants), SQL Agent job re-platforming (convert to pg_cron or external scheduler like Airflow), data migration via DMS or pgloader, dual-run validation, cutover, verify, and retire SQL Server. A rollback plan must exist. Risk factors: T-SQL procedural logic doesn't always map cleanly, SQL Server-specific features (linked servers, CLR procedures), and the application's Entity Framework LINQ provider may generate different SQL. Tools available: SSMA (SQL Server Migration Assistant), pgloader, AWS DMS, pgAdmin, SSMS, psql, dotnet EF tools.
